extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and their agents/representatives for PCT international-phase (international preliminary examination)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for how the International Preliminary Examining Authority conducts Chapter II (international preliminary) examination under the PCT and how applicants must respond (amendments, translations, sequence listings, unity, reports, timing, transmission and access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of amendments filed in another language
rubrics_metrics.description: Where amendments have been or are filed in another language, a translation of the amendments into the language in which the international preliminary examination is carried out must also be furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendments or accompanying letter are not in the required language, the International Preliminary Examining Authority will invite the applicant to furnish them within a reasonable time limit. If the applicant fails to furnish the amendments and/or the accompanying letter within the time limit set in the invitation, the Authority will not take the amendments into consideration for the purposes of the international preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document and translation request (Rule 66.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Authority needs a copy of an application the priority of which is claimed and the International Bureau already has it, the Bureau furnishes a copy to the Authority on request. If the applicant failed to provide the priority document under Rule 17.1, the international preliminary report may be established as if priority had not been claimed, but elected Offices may not later disregard priority without giving the applicant a reasonable opportunity to furnish it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the priority document is in a language other than the language(s) indicated for the Authority and the Authority considers validity of the priority claim relevant for novelty/inventive_step/industrial_applicability, the Authority may invite the applicant to furnish a translation in that language. The applicant must comply within two months; otherwise the report may be established as if priority had not been claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: To formulate a preliminary, non-binding opinion on whether the claimed invention appears (i) to be novel, (ii) to involve an inventive step (to be non‑obvious), and (iii) to be industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opinion is preliminary and non‑binding; national/regional Offices or courts will give the final opinion in the national phase. The Chapter II report gives a good idea of likely national results, although approaches vary among national laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty for international preliminary examination (Article 33(2), Rule 64)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention is considered novel if it is not anticipated by the prior art. Rule 64 defines prior art for the purposes of the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the definition of prior art as set out in Rule 64 when assessing anticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for international preliminary examination (Article 33(3), Rule 65)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention is considered to involve an inventive step if, having regard to the prior art as defined in the Regulations, it is not, at the prescribed relevant date, obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Rule 65 for further details on the application of the inventive step criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability for international preliminary examination (Article 33(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention is considered industrially applicable if, according to its nature, it can be made or used (in the technological sense) in any kind of industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents forming the basis of the international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination is based on the claims, the description and the drawings comprised in the international application. Amendments under Article 19 made before the demand and amendments under Article 34 are taken into account subject to timing and supersession rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments received after the Authority has begun to draw up a written opinion or the report need not be taken into account for those documents. Refer to paragraph 11.047 for permissibility of amendments in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims without international search report are excluded from examination (Rule 66.2(a)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims relating to inventions in respect of which no international search report has been established need not be the subject of international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any written opinion and the international preliminary report will indicate that those claims were not the subject of international preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top‑up search by the International Preliminary Examining Authority (Rule 66.1ter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority normally carries out a top‑up search to discover documents referred to in Rule 64 that were published or became available after the date of the international search report, unless it considers this would serve no useful purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report indicates whether a top‑up search was carried out and may include its results. The Authority may omit a top‑up search, for example where the application relates entirely to subject matter which is not required to be examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special requirements for nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings (Rule 13ter.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Authority finds the application contains disclosure of nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences that must be included in a sequence listing pursuant to Annex C and a compliant sequence listing in an accepted language has not been furnished, the Authority may invite the applicant to furnish such a listing or a translation of language‑dependent free text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listings required by the Authority are for the purposes of carrying out the international preliminary examination. National law requirements regarding sequence listings are matters for the national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority may comment that application is not required to be examined (Rule 66.2(a)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority notifies the applicant in a written opinion if it considers that the international application relates to subject matter on which it is not required to carry out an international preliminary examination, and decides not to carry out such an examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is similar to situations described in relation to the international search. The Authority may proceed no further for such subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority may comment on lack of clarity or inadequate support (Article 34(4)(a)(ii), Rule 66.2(a)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority may notify that the description, the claims or the drawings are so unclear, or the claims are so inadequately supported by the description, that no meaningful opinion can be formed on novelty, inventive_step or industrial_applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors procedures used in the international search; the written opinion will explain the reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority may indicate report should be negative for claims (Rule 66.2(a)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority may indicate that the international preliminary report on patentability should be 'negative' in respect of any claims because the claimed invention does not appear to be novel, does not appear to involve an inventive step, or does not appear to be industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written opinion and later the report will state reasons and cite relevant documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority may comment if an amendment goes beyond the disclosure (Rule 66.2(a)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority may notify the applicant if any amendment goes beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Authority considers amendments do not comply (introduce new matter), it will comment in the written opinion and the report may be established as if such amendment had not been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority may accompany report with unfavorable observations on clarity/support (Rule 66.2(a)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: The international preliminary report may be accompanied by unfavorable observations on the clarity of the claims, the description and the drawings, or on whether the claims are fully supported by the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority may decline to examine claims lacking ISR (Rule 66.2(a)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim relates to an invention in respect of which no international search report has been established, and the Authority decides not to carry out the international preliminary examination for that claim, it will so indicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraphs 7.013 to 7.021 for background on claims without ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority may notify inadequate sequence listing for meaningful exam (Rule 66.2(a)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listing is not available in such a form and language that a meaningful international preliminary examination can be carried out, the Authority may notify the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar procedure as in relation to the international search; the Authority may invite a compliant listing or translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: National law may limit multiple dependent claims (Rule 66.2(a) & paras 5.113, 7.014)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the national law applied by the Office acting as Authority does not allow multiple dependent claims to be drafted differently from Rule 6.4(a), the Authority will notify the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors notifications during the international search about multiple dependent claims drafted in a non‑permitted manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written opinion requirements (Rule 66.2, Rule 66.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'written opinion' is a notification by the Authority indicating comments on matters such as those listed in paragraph 10.064. The written opinion must fully state the reasons, invite the applicant to submit a written reply and fix a time limit for the reply (usually two months, extendible at the applicant's request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There may be no written opinion if the Authority has no comments; the Authority may issue one or more additional written opinions if time permits, particularly if the applicant makes a prompt and serious attempt to address comments by argument or amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's rights to react to a written opinion (Articles 34(2)(a),(d); Rules 66.2–66.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may ask for clarifications and may communicate orally or in writing with the Authority. The applicant may respond to a written opinion by amendments and/or arguments; responses may include oral communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any change other than rectification of obvious mistakes is considered an amendment. The form of amendments is governed by the rules (see paragraph 10.071); applicant may request additional opportunities for submitting amendments or arguments if time remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement for taking amendments/arguments into account (Rule 66.4bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and arguments will be taken into account if received in sufficient time. Amendments or arguments need not be taken into account for a written opinion or the report if they are received after the Authority has begun to draw up that opinion or report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given limited time for international preliminary examination, applicants should reply as soon as possible to any written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant not obliged to amend after negative written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority cannot force the applicant to make any change in the international application. The applicant may disregard any opinion wholly or in part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disregarding may lead to an unfavorable or less favorable international preliminary report, but the applicant may prefer this hoping to overcome difficulties in the national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments may not introduce new matter (Article 34(2)(b), Rule 70.2(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments under Article 34(2)(b) may not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed. If the Authority considers amendments do go beyond the disclosure, it will comment and the report will be established as if such amendment had not been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also reference paragraph 11.047 for general permissibility of amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for effecting amendments before the Authority (Rules 11.14,46.5,55.3,66.8,70.2(c-bis))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must submit a replacement sheet for every sheet which, due to an amendment, differs from the sheet previously filed. The amendment must be submitted with an accompanying letter explaining the difference and preferably the reasons, and must indicate the basis for the amendment in the application as originally filed. For claim amendments, a complete set of claims in replacement must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For deletions, minor alterations or additions, changes may be made on a copy of the relevant sheet provided clarity and direct reproducibility are not affected. No replacement sheet is required if an entire sheet is cancelled (a letter suffices). Amendments and accompanying letters must be in the language of publication (or of the translation on which the examination is based); translations are required where amendments filed in another language are to be taken into account. No fee is payable for Article 34(2)(b) amendments. Failure to furnish required accompanying letter may result in the Authority not taking the amendment into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention lacking — Authority's options (Rules 68,70.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Authority considers the application does not comply with unity of invention, it may carry out examination on the entire application and express views on lack of unity, or invite the applicant to restrict claims so they meet the requirement (specifying at least one possible restriction), or invite payment of additional fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant restricts, examination is carried out on restricted claims. If additional fees are paid, examination is carried out on the main invention and those claims for which fees were paid, and the report will indicate payment. Additional fees may be paid under protest. If applicant neither restricts nor pays, examination is carried out on the main invention as identified by the Authority or the applicant, or where in doubt the first mentioned invention in the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued significance of lack of unity in the national phase (Article 34(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A finding of lack of unity may remain important in the national phase. Any elected Office which agrees with the finding may require the applicant to restrict the claims, divide into divisional applications, or pay special fees to maintain parts not relating to the main invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Article 34(3) for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for establishment of the international preliminary report (Article 35(1), Rule 69.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must be established by whichever expires last: 28 months from the priority date; six months from the time provided under Rule 69.1 for the start of the international preliminary examination; or six months from receipt by the Authority of the translation furnished under Rule 55.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under normal circumstances the applicant receives the report at the latest two months before national processing may start, allowing time to decide on national phase entry and prepare actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and contents of the international preliminary report on patentability (Article 35, Rule 70)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report contains, among other things, a simple 'yes' or 'no' statement for each examined claim on whether it appears to satisfy novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability, accompanied where appropriate by citation of relevant documents with concise explanations and reasons for the Authority's conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report may include other matters listed earlier (e.g., unity remarks), indicate whether a top‑up search was carried out and its date or that none was made, and include concise explanations pointing out the criteria to which cited documents apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: How amendments are referenced in the international preliminary report (Rules 70.2(c-bis),70.2(e),70.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report identifies the basis on which it is established—i.e., whether, and if so which, amendments have been taken into account. If required accompanying letters were not submitted, the report may be established as if the amendments had not been made and will so indicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annexes to the report include replacement sheets containing amendments under Article 19 and/or Article 34 that have been taken into account and any accompanying letters, replacement sheets for rectifications of obvious mistakes and accompanying letters authorized under Rule 91, and may include superseded/reversed sheets in certain circumstances (e.g., where reversal/superseding amendments go beyond original disclosure or where required accompanying letters were not submitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on expressing national patentability views in the report (Article 35(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The international preliminary examination report shall not contain any statement on the question whether the claimed invention is or seems to be patentable or unpatentable according to any national law (including regional patent treaties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of the international preliminary report and translations (Rules 70.17,72,74)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report and any annexes are established in the language in which the international application is published, except where examination is carried out on the basis of a translation (then established in the language of that translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each elected State may require the report be translated into English; the International Bureau prepares the translation of the body of the report where required. If any elected Office requires translation of annexes, the applicant is responsible for preparing and furnishing those translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission and receipt of the report and translations (Articles 36, Rules 71,73,93bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority transmits, on the same day, copies of the report (and any annexes) to the applicant and the International Bureau. The International Bureau transmits copies to the elected Offices and a translation into English of the body of the report where required; the applicant must prepare translations of annexes if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant believes there are errors in the translation of the report, he/she may send written observations on such errors to any interested elected Office and must send a copy to the International Bureau. Comments on content should be addressed to elected Offices in the national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other documents in the Authority's file transmitted to the International Bureau (Rule 71.1(b), Section 602bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority also transmits copies of documents such as any written opinion, replacement sheets containing Article 34 amendments and accompanying letters (including superseded ones), any letters containing applicant's arguments under Rule 66.3, invitations to restrict or pay additional fees, protests and decisions thereon, and any other documents it wishes to transmit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents will be transmitted to the International Bureau generally not later than the time of transmittal of the report, but an Authority may decide to postpone transmittal until technically prepared to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility of the report and related documents (Articles 36,38; Rules 71,73,94)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report and related documents from the Authority's file are not published by the International Bureau; the Bureau communicates the report to elected Offices. However, if requested by an elected Office, the International Bureau will make the report available on PATENTSCOPE after expiration of 30 months from the priority date. Documents received or established by the Authority on or after 1 July 2020 will be made available on PATENTSCOPE after 30 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Authority may not give copies to anyone other than the applicant and the International Bureau unless requested/authorized by the applicant. Once the report becomes part of the file in the elected Office, national law governs access by third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining copies of documents cited in the international preliminary report (Article 36(4), Rule 71.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may obtain copies of those documents cited in the report which were not cited in the international search report by requesting them from the Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex E indicates the fees charged by such Authorities for furnishing copies on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and usefulness of the international preliminary report in the national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the report contains an opinion on compliance with internationally accepted criteria of novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability, it provides the applicant with a strong basis to evaluate the chances of obtaining patents in various Offices. While not binding on elected Offices, it carries considerable weight and a favorable report will assist prosecution before elected Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An elected Office identical to the Authority will generally proceed rapidly to grant in the national phase if the report is favorable.
